promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The six articles of faith (Sunni) and five roots of Usul ad-Din (Shi'a)
The nature of God (Tawhid), angels and predestination
Prophethood (Risalah), holy books, and Akhirah (life after death)

questions.q: How many articles of faith do Sunni Muslims traditionally accept?
questions.explain: Sunni Muslims hold six articles of faith, including belief in Tawhid, angels, holy books, prophets, the afterlife and predestination.

questions.q: The five roots of Usul ad-Din are the foundational beliefs of which group of Muslims?
questions.explain: The five roots of Usul ad-Din (Tawhid, Adl, Nubuwwah, Imamah and Mi'ad) are the core beliefs of Shi'a Islam.

questions.q: Which belief appears among the Shi'a five roots of Usul ad-Din but is NOT one of the Sunni six articles of faith?
questions.explain: Imamah, belief in the divinely appointed imams, is distinctive to Shi'a Islam and is not one of the Sunni six articles.

questions.q: What is the Islamic belief in the absolute oneness of God called?
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the oneness and unity of Allah, the most important teaching in Islam.

questions.q: Which angel is believed to have revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explain: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) delivered the revelations of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

questions.q: According to Islamic teaching, angels (malaikah) were created from what?
questions.explain: Angels are believed to be created from light and, unlike humans, have no free will and always obey God.

questions.q: Which angel is known in Islam as the angel of death?
questions.explain: Izra'il is the angel of death, responsible for taking souls at the end of life.

questions.q: Which prophet is regarded by Muslims as the final prophet, the 'Seal of the Prophets'?
questions.explain: Muhammad is believed to be the last and final prophet sent by Allah to all humanity.

questions.q: Which holy book do Muslims believe was given by God to the prophet Musa (Moses)?
questions.explain: The Tawrat (Torah) is believed to have been revealed by God to Musa.

questions.q: The Zabur (Psalms) is the holy book Muslims associate with which prophet?
questions.explain: Muslims believe the Zabur (Psalms) was given by God to the prophet Dawud (David).

questions.q: Which holy book do Muslims believe was originally revealed to the prophet Isa (Jesus)?
questions.explain: The Injil (Gospel) is the revelation Muslims believe was given to Isa, though they teach the original message was later altered.

questions.q: Surah 112 (Al-Ikhlas) of the Qur'an is best known for expressing which key Islamic belief?
questions.explain: Surah al-Ikhlas declares the absolute oneness of God, summarising the doctrine of Tawhid.

questions.q: What does the Sunni article of faith al-Qadr refer to?
options: God's predestination and control of all things
questions.explain: Al-Qadr is the belief that God has decreed and has knowledge of everything that happens.

questions.q: In Islam, the term Risalah is best understood as which of the following?
options: The channel of prophethood through which God communicates with humanity
The record of good and bad deeds
questions.explain: Risalah refers to prophethood, the means by which God sends his message to people through chosen prophets.

questions.q: In Islamic belief, what is Barzakh?
options: The state or barrier between death and the Day of Judgement
The book of a person's deeds
questions.explain: Barzakh is the intermediate state in which the soul waits between death and resurrection on the Day of Judgement.

questions.q: Which Islamic term refers to paradise?
questions.explain: Jannah is the Islamic term for paradise, the reward for the righteous after judgement.

questions.q: A Muslim refuses to worship anything or anyone alongside God, insisting worship belongs to Allah alone. Which belief most directly guides this action?
questions.explain: Tawhid, the oneness of God, means associating partners with God (shirk) is the gravest sin, so worship is due to Allah alone.

questions.q: A Muslim believes God already knows everything they will do, yet still feels fully responsible for their choices. Which article of faith does this reflect?
questions.explain: Al-Qadr teaches that God has knowledge of all things while humans remain accountable for their free choices on the Day of Judgement.

questions.q: A Muslim tries to behave well at all times because they believe angels are recording their good and bad deeds. This behaviour is shaped by belief in which article of faith?
questions.explain: Muslims believe angels such as the honourable recorders (Kiraman Katibin) write down each person's deeds, encouraging good conduct.

questions.q: A Muslim argues that after Muhammad the community needed divinely guided leaders to interpret the faith. This view most strongly reflects which of the Shi'a five roots?
questions.explain: Imamah is the Shi'a belief in a line of divinely appointed imams to lead and guide the Muslim community after Muhammad.

specSource: AQA GCSE Religious Studies A specification; Islam: Beliefs & Teachings
